output.question: When is SpaceX's IPO date?
output.answer: SpaceX already went public. The IPO priced on June 11, 2026 at $135 per share, and the stock started trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker SPCX on Friday, June 12, 2026. CNBC called it the biggest IPO ever: it raised about $75 billion, which valued SpaceX at about $1.77 trillion at the offer price. The shares opened at $150 and closed the first day at about $161, up 19%, for a market value of about $2.1 trillion. As of November 11, 2026 there is no IPO still to come, because SPCX is already a listed stock.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq on Friday, June 12, 2026, under the ticker SPCX.
The final IPO price of $135 per share was set on June 11, 2026.
At $135 per share the offering raised $75 billion, and SpaceX was valued at about $1.77 trillion at the IPO price.
The shares opened at $150 and closed the first day at about $161 (a later update gives $160.95), up 19%, valuing the company at about $2.1 trillion.
Musk and other insiders agreed to a 366-day lock-up. Other pre-IPO investors had a 180-day lock-up with staggered releases.

passages.quote: SpaceX jumped 19% on Friday in its Nasdaq debut after the biggest initial public offering ever.
The shares opened at $150 under the ticker SPCX after SpaceX raised $75 billion in the IPO.
The stock closed at around $161, valuing the company at $2.1 trillion.
The initial public offering (IPO) of SpaceX... occurred on June 12, 2026.
The final IPO price was $135 on June 11.

caveats: Sources disagree on how much the IPO raised. CNBC and most other outlets say $75 billion, while Wikipedia's lead section cites BBC for $86 billion. The higher figure may include the greenshoe (over-allotment) option, but I did not confirm that.
One TradingView page in the search results gave a planned IPO date of December 31, 2026. That conflicts with the June 12, 2026 listing reported by CNBC and others and looks out of date.

A third-party blog (Quantral) says the last insider lock-up expires December 8, but I did not open that page to check. Wikipedia describes a 366-day insider lock-up, which would point to a later date, so lock-up expiry dates are uncertain.
I did not open SpaceX's SEC prospectus or a Nasdaq release. The facts here come from CNBC and Wikipedia.
I did not check the current SPCX share price as of November 2026.
